# livekit_project_member (Resource)

A member of a **private** project (`is_private` on `data.livekit_project`) and their role. The user must already be a member of the project's workspace; `data.livekit_workspace_members` lists them. A project that is not private takes its members from its workspace, where a change would reach every project in it, so this resource refuses one. It also refuses to remove the user the session belongs to, and a member who owns API keys in the project: removing them would delete their keys. An existing member is adopted only through import.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Give a member of the workspace read access to a private project.
data "livekit_workspace_members" "all" {}

locals {
  users = { for m in data.livekit_workspace_members.all.members : m.email => m.user_id }
}

resource "livekit_project_member" "support" {
  user_id = local.users["support@example.com"]
  role    = "read"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `role` (String) The member's role: `read`, `write` or `admin`. A plan that allows only admins refuses the others.
- `user_id` (String) ID of the user. Changing it replaces the membership.

### Optional

- `project_id` (String) Project (`p_...`) the membership belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the membership is created; a later change of that default does not move it. Changing this argument replaces the membership.

### Read-Only

- `email` (String) The user's email address.
- `id` (String) `<project_id>/<user_id>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a membership by "<project_id>/<user_id>".
terraform import livekit_project_member.support p_abc123/U1a2b3c4d5e6f
```
